claims.explanation: Thiocolchicoside is a colchicine-site tubulin binder whose anticancer selectivity is best explained by the tubulin/microtubule and apoptosis machinery of each line rather than by its annotated GABA/glycine receptor targets, which are not expressed in most solid tumors. Lines with intact or amplified microtubule-dependent survival signaling and wild-type TP53-independent apoptosis (e.g., high TUBB3/TUBB expression, low ABCB1 efflux, or SMARCA4/ARID1A loss) are sensitized, whereas lines with high multidrug efflux or strong anti-apoptotic tone are protected.

features.basis: High beta-III tubulin increases colchicine-site drug binding and mitotic arrest
P-glycoprotein efflux lowers intracellular thiocolchicoside
SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434) are enriched among selective killers
ARID1A loss appears in multiple selectively killed lines
TP53-mutant lines are common among least-affected lines
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines appear among selective killers
NFE2L2-mutant squamous lines are enriched among selective killers
Annotated GABA-A target; expression may buffer drug response
Thiocolchicoside downregulates Bcl-2; high Bcl-2 blunts apoptosis
NF-kB pathway activity is required for thiocolchicoside anticancer effect
CDKN2A loss is enriched among least-affected lines
